extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive synthetic framework for evaluating retrieval and reasoning in bilingual long-context tasks across adaptive context lengths. It includes information-sparse retrieval tasks and an information-dense Ancestral Trace Challenge to test long-context understanding and reasoning.
extraction.creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark that programmatically constructs long-context tasks by inserting key data points (“needles”) into background text (“haystack”). The benchmark includes information-sparse tasks with irrelevant filler content and an information-dense Ancestral Trace Challenge where every sentence contains critical information. English haystacks are built from PaulGrahamEssays passages, and Chinese haystacks from ChineseDomainModelingEval.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Background/filler text from PaulGrahamEssays for English tasks and ChineseDomainModelingEval for Chinese tasks; synthetic needles consisting of fabricated facts and kinship relations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks; the models still struggle on information-sparse long-context retrieval/reasoning, and performance degrades as reasoning steps increase.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to identify and address gaps in LLM long-context retrieval and reasoning, with future work suggested to improve reasoning strategies and mitigate under-thinking.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of large language models on retrieval and reasoning tasks in long-context scenarios; the paper also evaluates models at 32K and 128K context lengths.
